newsitem.title: UK: Mideast/Japan dirty tanker rates up on good fixing.
newsitem.headline: Mideast/Japan dirty tanker rates up on good fixing.

text.p: Dirty tanker rates for VLCCs crept higher on Wednesday amid good demand for tonnage as more product moved east than west, shipping brokers said.
"We have seen W70 for a (250,000 tonne) ULCC and that may be the new trend," one said. The 250,000 tonne Golden Stream was fixed at W68.75, in line with fixtures earlier in the week.
"I thought it would be lower but it all comes down to dates," he said, adding that he saw the market at around W67.5
Mideast/west fixing was less active. Vela fixed two 280,000 tonners to make westwards journeys from mid December and paid W52.5 for US Gulf destinations.

Cross-Med markets were steady at W105 for 80,000 tonne Aframax tankers and slightly weaker at W90-W92.5 for 130,000 tonne Suezmaxes. Exxon's cross-Med chartering of the 80,000 tonne Montrose at just below W120 was above market because of a scarcity of appropriate vessels for the timing required, and this ship needed a longer ballast for the voyage.
"A more general rate would be W105," a broker said. Med Suezmax rates have been softening, however, as maintenance at Novorossiisk's Suezmax terminal reduces the level of fixing.
Caribs/U.S. Gulf routes were holding this week's strength amid a dearth of ships.
Brokers said increased fixing ahead of the U.S. thanksgiving holiday on Thursday had also prompted a scramble for vessels which was holding rates for 70,000 tonners up at W135-W140.
West Africa/US markets were steady with a flurry of million-barrel fixtures done between W95 and W102.5. North Sea fixtures for journeys across the Atlantic were steady at around W107.5.
But rates were slipping for Aframaxes making cross-Continent voyages. Latest fixtures were done at around W97.5 but brokers thought this could fall by a couple of points in the coming days.
